stories.title: China calls for Middle East dialogue in talks with Iran, Saudi Arabia, Oman
summary: Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security”, Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri Kani, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.
China’s foreign ministry had not previously announced the visit by Bagheri Kani to Beijing.

Later this month, Beijing will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia as part of “shuttle diplomacy visits… aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions”, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson told a news briefing.

stories.title: Adrian Hamilton-Manns appointed new PIA chief executive officer
summary: The board of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) on Monday announced the appointment of Adrian Hamilton-Manns as its chief executive officer (CEO).

In a press release, PIA said Hamilton-Manns “brings a wealth of leadership and strategic experience within the global aviation sector”, adding that his appointment “marks a pivotal chapter” in the airline’s ongoing transformation.
A consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited had won the auction for 75 per cent shares of PIA in December last year, making a winning bid of Rs135 billion.

stories.title: CDF Munir discusses 'evolving regional, international security dynamics' with Chinese dignitary
summary: Besides discussing matters of mutual interest, both sides “expressed their shared resolve to further strengthen the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between Pakistan and China”, ISPR said.

China’s Haixing appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence in further advancing the longstanding strategic partnership between the two countries, according to the statement.
Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership rooted in mutual trust, economic cooperation and regional connectivity.

stories.title: PM directs no leniency for banks slow in providing loans to farmers, SMEs
summary: Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif on Monday directed that no leniency should be shown to banks who were slow in providing loans to farmers, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and consumers under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar Scheme.
The scheme was launched by the prime minister in April, under which housing and construction loans of up Rs10 million were to be given on easy instalments.
The meeting was briefed that significant progress had been made by the SBP in providing loans on a priority basis to housing, agriculture, and SMEs.

stories.title: Political committee denies 'factionalism' within PTI, warns against violating party discipline
summary: The warning was issued by PTI’s political committee, which deliberated on party matters and the country’s overall situation.

According to a statement shared on X, the political committee clarified there “is no grouping or division in the party”. “The entire party is united with Imran Khan’s leadership, his ideology and his mission.

The committee also expressed “serious” reservations over the alleged arrests of party leaders and workers, particularly actions taken under MPO, and urged that no one be “targeted for revenge on the basis of political differences”.

stories.title: Pakistan Broadcasters Association elects new board directors, office-bearers
summary: The Pakistan Broadcasters Association (PBA) held its annual general body meeting on Friday to elect new members.
According to a press release, a majority of members from the TV and radio industry were present during the annual general body meeting in Karachi.
During the meeting, the general body elected three TV members as directors on the PBA board in the elected member category.

stories.title: Civilian convicted of offences against state cannot claim fundamental rights, govt says in report to LHC
summary: It accused him of concealing facts about his appeal, his father Hafeezullah Khan Niazi’s earlier proceedings, including a petition before the apex court and a contempt petition, as well as the anti-terrorism court’s May 25, 2023, order.
The report said Niazi had not annexed the military court’s order, an objection upheld by the high court in two other petitions.

The reply said that Niazi, held at Kot Lakhpat Jail, was convicted by a Field General Court Martial (FGCM) and sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment under Section 3 of the Official Secrets Act, 1923, read with Section 59 of the Army Act.

stories.title: Consumer inflation falls to 9.6pc in Oct from 10.3pc in Sept
summary: The slowdown in the inflation rate for the second consecutive month, measured by the Consumer Price Index, reversed the sharp increase recorded in August, when higher food and energy prices pushed the annual rate to 11.1pc from 9.2pc in July.
Food inflation dropped to 7.8pc in urban areas in October from 8.1pc in September.
The decline was much sharper in rural areas, where food inflation fell to 7.1pc from 7.7pc a month earlier.

stories.title: Pakistan fined for slow over-rate in tri-series final
summary: Pakistan have been fined five per cent of their match fees for maintaining a slow over-rate during their three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the One-day International tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday.

Pakistan had conceded 325-8 in the final before chasing down the target of 326 with three wickets and nine balls to spare, securing the tri-series title in front of their home crowd at Gaddafi Stadium.
His innings helped Pakistan recover from an early collapse and complete a joint-record successful chase in an ODI final.

stories.title: On eve of midterms, final polls point to Democratic gains, but can Republicans hold the Senate?
summary: Of the 100 seats in the Senate, Fox considers Democrats favoured in 48 Senate seats and Republicans in 45, with seven competitive states likely to determine control of the chamber.
Republicans believe that voters who supported him in those states could return to the polls and support Republican Senate candidates, even if the national political environment has shifted.

The network’s analysis presents two possible scenarios: a Democratic gain that could give the party as many as 55 Senate seats, or a Republican performance strong enough to preserve a majority of up to 52.

stories.title: LHC directs jail authorities to arrange meeting between Noreen Niazi, her daughters
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday directed jail authorities to arrange a meeting between Noreen Niazi, the sister of PTI founder Imran Khan, and her two daughters on Tuesday (tomorrow).
Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the directives while hearing petitions challenging the extensions in the detention orders of Imran’s sisters Noreen, Uzma Khan and Aleema Khanum.
Aleema and Noreen, along with their sister Uzma Khan, were detained under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 in September, as the PTI geared up for a protest march to Islamabad.

stories.title: Dear Test cricket, I stayed up
summary: South African captain Temba Bavuma ducks a bouncer during the third Test against Australia at the Newlands Stadium.–AFP Chapter Four: Wednesday Day two Simon Harmer has Travis Head chopping on for 41.
South African all-rounder Wiaan Mulder runs between the wickets.–AFP Chapter Six: Saturday Morning Day five Kagiso Rabada has the new ball.
Starc, promoted to number eight to deal with the footmarks, survives 25 balls without scoring and is caught at bat-pad off the last ball before lunch, the longest duck of his Test career.

stories.title: Babar, Shaheen set for Quaid-e-Azam Trophy opening-round clash
summary: Abdullah Shafique will captain Sialkot Blues, while Mohammad Nawaz has been named skipper of Rawalpindi in the Silver tier.
Eight teams will compete in the Gold tier, with Karachi Blues, Faisalabad, Fata, Lahore Whites, Islamabad, Peshawar Blues, Multan and Sialkot Blues vying for the title.
In the Gold tier, Lahore Whites’ squad includes Babar, all-rounder Aamir Jamal, Tayyab Tahir and Noman Ali, while Fata will be led by Shaheen and also feature Khushdil Shah and Mohammad Wasim Khan.

stories.title: Bangladesh garment workers protesting for higher wages clash with police
summary: Thousands of Bangladeshi garment workers blocked a major highway and clashed with police on Monday, demanding a monthly minimum wage more than double their current pay, as protests spread across industrial hubs.
Garment workers gather to protest demanding higher minimum wages in Dhaka on November 2, 2026. — AFP Angry workers also set fire to a police vehicle.

The protests came despite the government’s announcement on Sunday that it would establish a wage board to review the minimum wage in the vital garment industry, which employs millions of people and generates the bulk of Bangladesh’s export earnings.

stories.title: Laden with eggs, robots race up sacred Chinese mountain
summary: Dozens of robots took on more than 3,000 steps up one of China’s most famous peaks on Monday, carrying eggs and watermelons in a race organisers billed as a test of real-world machine endurance, state media showed.
The fastest humanoid robot — belonging to Beijing-based team Zhishen Lingyue — completed a shorter race course in 27 minutes and 26 seconds.
The race, organised by the state-run China Media Group, featured cash prizes for winners in several categories, including the fastest robots and the best load-carrying four-legged machine.

stories.title: Islamabad court sentences man to 7-year jail term for filming objectionable video of teenage boy
summary: An Islamabad Additional District and Sessions Court sentenced Raja Haris Naveed to seven years of rigorous imprisonment in a cybercrime case involving the harassment of a 16-year-old boy and the recording of an objectionable video without his consent, it emerged on Monday.
Read: Two held for involvement in child abuse case In case of non-payment of the fine, the judge said the convict will have to serve an additional six months in prison.
In a similar case, an Islamabad court on October 22 sentenced two men to 10 years in prison each for blackmailing a 12-year-old girl and sharing her objectionable pictures.

stories.title: Adrian Hamilton-Manns formally takes charge as PIA's new CEO
summary: Adrian Hamilton-Manns has formally assumed charge as the new chief executive officer (CEO) of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), bringing three decades of commercial aviation experience to the national flag carrier.
He brings a wealth of leadership & strategic experience, and his appointment marks a pivotal chapter in PIA’s ongoing transformation," the airline said in a statement posted on X on Monday.
PIA' Board is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Adrian Hamilton-Manns as the CEO.

stories.title: US midterms: Michigan Democrat's endorsement of Republican ruffles critical Senate race
summary: A prominent Michigan Democrat endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday, giving President Donald Trump’s Republicans an unexpected boost in ​a critical US Senate race two days before midterm elections that will decide control of Congress.
He declined to directly address Stevens’ endorsement on Sunday. “This race was never about me,” El-Sayed told MS NOW. “It was never even about Mike Rogers.

Alaska Intervention Falters Also on Sunday, the Trump administration’s attempt to intervene in Alaska’s Senate race faltered when a federal judge dismissed the US Justice Department’s lawsuit seeking to block certification of the results if Republican incumbent Senator Dan S.

stories.title: Oil refineries to bear Rs15b burden to ease fuel price pressure leading to Rs15 cut in petrol price
summary: The government on Monday announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Speaking about Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's approach to providing relief to consumers, Malik said the government was providing relief to the people according to its means.

Apart from the fuel relief scheme that was offering "targeted relief" to 13 million people, the government had undertaken several other measures to alleviate the burden on the masses, the petroleum minister stated.

stories.title: Lahore's air quality index crosses 530 as pollution reaches hazardous levels
summary: Several other cities in Punjab also recorded extremely high pollution levels, according to air quality monitoring platform IQAir.

Figure shows the top ranked polluted cities in Pakistan according to IQAir on Friday morning. — Screengrab via IQAir The worsening air quality comes amid a sharp increase in agricultural fire detections across Punjab.

Weather factor Meanwhile, a new analysis by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI) has questioned the extent of improvement in Lahore’s air quality during October, despite government claims that the city experienced its cleanest October in five years.

stories.title: AI models mostly smarter than top scientists, OpenAI's Altman says
summary: Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models have progressed to become mostly smarter than the brightest scientists and capable of performing significant portions of white-collar work, OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said on Monday.
Altman stressed that despite the disruptive impact on global economies and employment, human judgement, creativity and accountability must remain central to the technology's deployment.

During the event, OpenAI announced partnerships with Emirati technology group G42 and state oil producer Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, marking the first global deployment of OpenAI's frontier models by an energy company.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz directs SBP, FBR to resolve tax issues faced by SMEs, exporters
summary: The PMO said that during the meeting, officials briefed the prime minister that the SBP was working on three main pillars to increase lending to priority sectors: improving regulations, sharing risks and costs between the government and banks, and expanding digital facilities.
The meeting was informed that, as of October 23, loans worth Rs511 billion had been approved under the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Programme, covering 86,899 applications.
The government had set a target of increasing lending to both the agriculture and SME sectors to Rs1,500 billion by the end of fiscal year 2027, officials said.

stories.title: Israeli forces fire tear gas at Palestinian students, teachers in West Bank as occupiers block roads
summary: Dozens of Palestinian students and teachers suffered suffocation from Israeli tear gas on Monday, as occupiers blocked several roads in the latest escalation in the occupied West Bank.
Earlier Monday, the Palestinian Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission said Israeli occupiers carried out 1,369 attacks across the West Bank in October, up 111.6% from 647 in September.
Nearly 750,000 Israeli occupiers live in 156 illegal settlements and around 360 outposts across the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, according to Palestinian figures.

stories.title: Jordan’s king calls Israel's expansionist ambitions ‘biggest threat’ to region’s future
summary: He pointed to the continuing humanitarian catastrophe in the Gaza Strip and Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, despite international calls to halt Israeli violations.

Read: 2 Palestinians killed in Israel's ongoing violations of Gaza ceasefire He reaffirmed Jordan’s commitment to its principles, Arab identity and defending Arab causes, pledging to maintain that position as his father had before him and his son would after him.
Israeli military operations and attacks by illegal occupiers have also intensified in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

stories.title: Aashir Wajahat sparks 'Parwarish' reunion speculation with Samar Jafri, Abul Hassan
summary: Aashir Wajahat has fuelled speculation about a possible reunion of the Parwarish team after sharing a picture with fellow actors Samar Jafri and Abul Hassan, alongside the drama's director, Syed Meesam Naqvi.

View this post on Instagram Fans were quick to flood the comments section with excitement, with one user expressing disbelief at the prospect of seeing the three actors together in a drama directed by Meesam. “SAMAR, AASHIR, ABUL IN A DRAMA THAT TOO DIRECTED BY MEESAM SIR?
Jafri and Hassan previously appeared together in the hit drama Parwarish, which premiered in April 2025.

stories.title: Israel maintains highest state of alert on eve of US midterm elections
summary: Israel remained on the highest state of military alert on Monday, a day before the United States midterm elections, amid concerns over a possible resumption of war with Iran, according to Israeli media.

Trump has repeatedly pledged not to launch new strikes against Iran before the midterm elections, while suggesting that military operations could resume afterward, amid a continued US military buildup in the region and stalled diplomatic efforts.

Israeli news website Walla reported Monday that the military remained on high alert amid US and Israeli concerns that Iran could launch a surprise attack, either directly or through allied groups, against American interests in the region or Israel.

stories.title: Merub Ali praises Dananeer, Romaisa Khan for proving their talent beyond social media
summary: Merub Ali has praised the growing presence of social media influencers in the entertainment industry, pointing to fellow actors Dananeer Mobeen and Romaisa Khan as examples of digital creators who have successfully made the transition to television.
Speaking about Mobeen, Ali described her as a prime example of how social media could help talented newcomers find opportunities in showbiz. “I just believe in talent.
Ali also praised Khan, who built a substantial online following through her social media content before establishing herself as a television actor. “Romaisa is also a beautiful actress.

stories.title: Governor Kundi says Centre failing to give KP support it deserves
summary: Says collective efforts needed to restore province’s positive image He stated that improvement of health infrastructure, provision of modern medical equipment, doctors’ training and promotion of medical research were essential for strengthening healthcare system.
Meanwhile, during his address at Darbar-i-Aalia Murshadabad Sharif in the provincial capital, the governor said that lasting peace was essential for the province’s progress and prosperity.

In a statement issued from his office, the governor emphasised the need for unity, lasting peace, development, promotion of sports, effective utilisation of the province’s natural resources and collective efforts to ensure welfare and prosperity of the people.

stories.title: Tarar announces plans to revive PTV Drama, Film Academy
summary: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Monday announced plans to restore and modernise the Pakistan Television (PTV) Drama and Film Academy, aiming to equip young people with contemporary filmmaking and digital production skills.

By bringing specialised training facilities to Pakistan and involving private-sector partners and universities, the initiative aims to help bridge the skills gap and prepare a new generation of professionals for opportunities in the evolving media landscape.

stories.title: 3 killed, at least 29 injured in shootings near US college communities
summary: In Newark, Delaware, at least six people were hospitalised following a shooting Saturday night on Main Street near the University of Delaware.

Read: 1 killed, 6 injured in shooting at Halloween store in California In Birmingham, Alabama, one person was killed and eight others wounded near Legion Field following the Magic City Classic football game between Alabama A&M and Alabama State.
In Bloomington, Illinois, a 19-year-old woman was killed, and seven others hospitalised after shots were fired near Illinois Wesleyan University shortly before 1.25 am Sunday.

stories.title: US midterms: Polls show Democrats ahead in battle for Congress
summary: Democrats lead Republicans in national polling ahead of Tuesday's United States midterm elections, with new surveys showing the party gaining ground in several closely contested Senate races as voters express dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump's handling of the economy.
A RealClearPolling average of surveys conducted through October 30 shows Democrats leading Republicans 52% to 43.1% on the generic congressional ballot, an 8.9-percentage-point advantage.

The latest New York Times/Siena University polls, conducted from October 23-November 1, show Democratic candidates ahead in six of seven key Senate battlegrounds and effectively tied with Republicans in the seventh.

stories.title: KP doctors oppose amendments to Pharmacy Act 1967
summary: The PMDC upholds this authority in its rules and licensing framework,” Dr Rizwan said.

He added that the delegation had also asked the prime minister to order an inquiry into Category-B health education institutions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to identify alleged irregularities in the awarding of degrees.

Dr Rizwan said Dr Shaista and other members of the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on National Health Services assured the delegation that its concerns would be taken up in their meeting for remedial measures accordingly.

stories.title: LHC recognises daily-wage employees as permanent workers in Punjab health authorities
summary: The court relied on the Supreme Court's ruling in Province of Punjab vs Ahmad Hussain (2013 SCMR 1547), which recognised that daily-wage and work-charged employees continuously performing work of a permanent nature beyond nine months could acquire the status of permanent workmen.

Also read: NA resolution on workplace harassment The employees had produced departmental orders showing that similarly placed daily-wage workers had already been granted permanent-workman status in various districts.

The ruling reinforces the legal protections available to long-serving daily-wage and work-charged employees in Punjab's public health system, requiring the concerned authorities to implement the government's policy in accordance with labour laws.

stories.title: Man sentenced to life for assaulting minor sister-in-law
summary: PESHAWAR: Peshawar High Court has set aside the acquittal of a medical doctor and sentenced him to life imprisonment with fine of Rs500,000 for sexually assaulting his 12-year-old sister-in-law over three years ago.
A bench consisting of Justice Sahibzada Asadullah and Justice Inamullah Khan accepted an appeal filed by the victim and declared that the trial court had erred in acquitting the suspect.
PHC accepts appeal of victim, sets aside acquittal order of trial court An additional sessions judge/child protection court had acquitted the suspect on Nov 11, 2025 in the case.

stories.title: Police set up eight pickets for PAF base security in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: Eight special police pickets have been set up at various locations to ensure the security of the PAF base.

As part of the security plan for the eight pickets, police mobile squads from Chaklala, Sadiqabad and Waris Khan police stations will patrol around Nur Khan PAF Base, while the Muhafiz Squad and Dolphin Force have been assigned patrol duties around the base.
At the TM Chowk police picket, the RA Bazaar police, Muhafiz Squad and Dolphin Force will patrol within the limits of the R.A.

stories.title: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority appoints three new directors general
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has completed the recruitment process for three new directors general (DGs) in BS-20.
According to CDA officials, retired Brig Mohammad Javed Iqbal, retired Brig Rashid Manzoor and retired Brig Azhar Khan have been appointed as DGs.
However, after the stay was vacated, the CDA completed the recruitment process and issued notifications appointing the new DGs.

stories.title: Jhelum's ancient Padhri village faces relentless erosion
summary: Located at the foot of Tilla Jogian, Padhri village is another place dotted with astonishing examples of stone architecture typical of the Salt Range terrain.

Syed Ahmed, another resident, while guiding this correspondent through the streets, said all the houses had been built with grey stones brought from the surrounding hills of Tarakki, Domeli and Tilla Jogian.
A centuries-old small mosque, featuring a highly attractive facade built with sandy grey stones, is another marvel of stone craftsmanship in the Domeli and Tilla region.

stories.title: 120 Swabi schools sealed over poor building conditions
summary: SWABI: The district administration has sealed around 120 schools, mostly private, in different parts of Swabi after inspections revealed that their buildings were unsafe for students, sources said on Sunday.

The sources told Dawn that inspections conducted in all four tehsils of the district found cracks in the walls and rooms of several school buildings, making them unfit for educational activities and posing a threat to students’ lives.
The deputy commissioner said the district had a total of 289,180 students, adding that the administration did not have separate figures for children enrolled in private schools.

stories.title: Messi inspires Miami comeback against New England
summary: Lionel Messi's late strike catapulted Inter Miami above New England and into second place with a tense 2-1 comeback victory over their MLS Eastern Conference rivals Sunday.
Victory sent Miami a point clear of the New England Revolution with one game left, meaning a win against Charlotte on Saturday will guarantee home advantage until the Conference Finals.
Nashville lifted the Supporters' Shield trophy on Sunday at their Geodis Park stadium, where they have not lost all year, becoming the first team in MLS history with 15 home wins.

stories.title: CM inaugurates Rs250m Sindhi Muslim Food Walk
summary: According to an official statement, the urban improvement project aims to promote food and cultural tourism, facilitating local businesses, improving civic infrastructure and providing residents and visitors with a better environment to enjoy the city’s rich culinary culture.
The chief minister said Sindhi Muslim was already among Karachi’s well-known commercial and food destinations, attracting visitors from different parts of the city.

He said the Food Walk was not merely a beautification scheme but a comprehensive urban improvement initiative designed to make the area more accessible, attractive, organised and convenient for businesses, visitors and residents.
